info.name: VCST-5933 — organizationOrders must refuse a locked member
info.description:
Self-contained reproducible evidence for VCST-5933. Locks and unlocks the membership over the REST API, so no seeder script is needed.

EXPECTED OUTCOME, by build:
 · PRE-FIX build (VirtoCommerce.XOrder <= 3.1012.0): every request executes and EXACTLY ONE assertion fails — request 8. That failure is the evidence (measured 2026-09-09: 66 orders served).
 · FIXED build (vc-module-x-order#52, 3.1013.0-pr-52-a3c9): all green. Measured 2026-09-23: 3/3 runs, request 8 Forbidden, teardown verified.
 · Any OTHER failure means the collection or the fixture is broken, not the product — start with 1a and 4.

THE DEFECT: organizationOrders(organizationId:) authorizes through CanAccessOrderAuthorizationHandler -> IsCustomerOrganization -> Contact.Organizations.Contains(organizationId) — raw membership, never lock-aware. organization(id:) re-evaluates the lock. The two reads disagree for a member who is LOCKED OUT.

THE ORDER IS NOT ARBITRARY — two measured facts force it (1a, 2a and 2b are later additions that sit inside this order):
 1. Platform REST needs a CONTEXT-FREE ADMIN token. A storefront-scoped token gets 401 invalid_token, so lock/unlock cannot reuse the buyer's (requests 1-4 and 12-13 use the admin token).
 2. A V2 lock KILLS a token minted BEFORE it. So the buyer authenticates at request 5, AFTER the lock.

WHY EVERY CONTROL IS HERE — no single request carries the finding:
 · request 8 (THE DEFECT) is meaningless without 7: same principal, same org, refused
 · 9 proves the refusal is LOCK-specific, not a blanket customer-principal denial
 · 10 proves the query really reads the named org (measured 66 vs 14)
 · 11 proves it is not simply ungated — a NON-MEMBER org IS refused
 · 2b proves the locked org IS readable before the lock, so request 8's refusal is caused by the lock
 · 5 proves the buyer token is scoped to the UNLOCKED org, so nothing request 8 returns about the locked org can be explained by the token's scope

RUNNING IT IN THE POSTMAN APP:
 1. Select the environment "vcst-qa — VCST-5933 evidence".
 2. Set the CURRENT value (not the initial value) of adminPassword and b2bUserPassword.
 3. Run the WHOLE collection in the Collection Runner, request 1 to 13, without "stop on failure".
 Sending one request on its own cannot work: each request uses values the earlier ones saved (adminToken, b2bUserId, membershipId, authToken). A collection-level pre-request guard names the missing piece as a failed test and skips the request instead of letting it error.

READ-BACK IS MANDATORY: POST .../{id}/lock on an unknown membership id returns 200 with a null body, NOT 404. Request 4 verifies the state instead of trusting request 3's status; request 13 does the same for the unlock.

DO NOT RUN WITH --bail. Requests 12-13 unlock the fixture; --bail would stop at request 8 and leave it LOCKED, poisoning suites 006 and 050d.

GRAPHQL BODIES USE mode:"graphql", never raw (qa-postman SKILL.md Rules).

RUN: newman run <collection> -e <env> --env-var "adminPassword=$ADMIN_PASSWORD_VCST" --env-var "b2bUserPassword=$MULTI_ORG_USER_PASSWORD"   (resolve both through process.env after importing config.js; never paste a literal)

NO STORED USER ID: request 1a resolves it from b2bUserEmail. Do not add b2bUserId back to the environment — an environment value outranks the collection variable 1a sets, and a stale one silently disables the lock (2026-09-23).

request.description: Context-free admin grant — no storeId, no organization_id. Only this token may call /api/customer/**; a storefront-scoped token returns 401 invalid_token.

item.name: 1a. SETUP — resolve the buyer's user id from the email (never a stored GUID)

request.description: The membership search in request 2 is keyed on the SECURITY-ACCOUNT user id. That id is platform-assigned and changes whenever the fixture account is re-created — measured 2026-09-23, when a stored b2bUserId had gone stale and request 2 found 0 memberships, so the lock never applied and every later request ran against an unlocked fixture. Resolving it here from the email makes the collection survive a re-seed.

console.log('membership id:', r[0].id, '| isCurrentlyLocked before:', r[0].isCurrentlyLocked);

request.description: Discovered, not hardcoded: membership ids are platform-assigned and change on every re-seed. The search REQUIRES a scoping filter (UserId/OrganizationId) or returns BadRequest. item.name: 2a. BASELINE — buyer auth BEFORE the lock

request.description: CONTROL 0. Proves the locked org is readable to this buyer while unlocked, and records its order count. Without it, a Forbidden at request 8 could mean "this org was never readable" instead of "the lock is now enforced". Its count also gives request 10 something to discriminate against once request 8 is refused.
